column1: # The data build of the 30B baseline arm, one line per corpus, consumed by
# configs/control_pretraining/build_corpora.sh (which submits the jobs and reimplements nothing).
#   subset | stage | kind | config | prep_h | tok_h | workers | shards | shard_mode | stripe | docs
#   kind        tokenize -> .bin/.idx via pipeline_data_submit.sbatch tokenize
#               pack     -> packed SFT parquet via pipeline_data_submit.sbatch <root> (pack-only)
#   config      the prepare config (dataset, revision, tokenizer) the corpus is an instance of
#   prep_h/tok_h  walltimes in hours, sized from the corpus's parquet volume and V1's measurements
#               (ClimbMix prepare took 5.1 h for the same document count, so the sbatch default
#               of 4 h would have killed it); workq_qos caps any job at 24 h
#   workers     tokenize worker count
#   shard_mode  none  -> one prepare + one tokenize/pack
#               split -> one prepare, then shard_jsonl_corpus.sh cuts the JSONL into `shards`
#                        byte-gated roots, then one tokenize/pack per shard
#               slice -> `shards` prepares of contiguous HuggingFace index ranges straight into
#                        the shard roots (needs the exact `docs`), then one tokenize per shard
#   stripe      1 for corpora big enough that a single OST is a read bottleneck; applied to the
#               dataset root BEFORE prepare writes training.jsonl
#   docs        the subset's exact document count (PENDING until known; slice needs it, and
#               verify_corpora.py checks every built corpus against it)
# ClimbMix is the one corpus a single writer cannot finish inside a 24 h window (README:
# "Why ClimbMix is sharded"). It is source-SLICED — eight prepares of contiguous index ranges
# straight into the shard roots, each tokenized as soon as its own prepare lands — which is
# how the shipped corpus was built (README: "The shipped ClimbMix was built by
# source-slicing"): each step is ~1 h instead of the split path's 7.5 h prepare, and the
# separate split job with its ~1.7 TB peak disappears. `split` remains available for a corpus
# whose exact document count is unknown; the two cut different shard boundaries.
